name: Swimming
summary: A whole-body cardiovascular exercise performed in water using rhythmic arm strokes and flutter or whip kicks for propulsion.

setup: Enter the pool lane and align your body horizontally in the water.
Push off the wall into a streamlined prone position with your core engaged and head neutral.
steps: Propel forward by alternating arm strokes, pulling water beneath your torso and recovering the arms above the surface.
Maintain a steady, compact kick from the hips with relaxed ankles to stabilize body position.
Rotate along your long axis smoothly with each stroke cycle, turning your head to the side to inhale as needed without lifting it excessively.
Touch or flip-turn at the pool wall to transition smoothly into the next length.
instructions.breathing: Exhale continuously into the water and rotate your head into the stroke's bow wave to inhale quickly and rhythmically.
cues: Kick from the hips, not the knees
Reach long and pull through the water
Rotate the body as a single unit

common_faults.fault: Lifting the head high out of the water to breathe, which causes the hips and legs to sink.
common_faults.correction: Keep one goggle lens in the water while breathing, rotating the head alongside the torso rather than lifting it forward.

common_faults.fault: Kicking excessively from the knees with large, drag-inducing movements.
common_faults.correction: Generate kick propulsion from the hips and glutes with loose ankles and relatively straight legs.

precautions: Swim only in designated lanes or areas supervised by a qualified lifeguard.
Stop immediately if experiencing calf cramps, extreme fatigue, or dizziness.
